testCases.input: What do the docs say about the difference between fine-tuning and prompting?
testCases.actualOutput:
**What the OpenAI documentation says about the difference between fine‑tuning and prompting** | Aspect | Fine‑tuning (custom model) | Prompting (prompt engineering) | |--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------| | **What it does** | Adjusts the model’s weights by training on a user‑provided dataset. The result is a *new* model that “remembers” the patterns in that data. | Leaves the model’s weights unchanged. You steer the model’s behavior only by the text you send in the request (the prompt). | | **When to use it** | • You need *persistent* behavior that should apply to every request without re‑specifying instructions.
• You have a sizable, high‑quality dataset that captures the domain‑specific knowledge or style you want.
• You want lower latency per request (the model is already specialized). | • You need a quick, ad‑hoc solution or want to experiment with different instructions.
• Your use case can be expressed with a few examples or a clear instruction set.
• You don’t have enough data (or the budget) to create a fine‑tuned model. | | **Cost & latency** | One‑time training cost (based on token count of the training set) plus the cost of using
